# Course Schedule {.unnumbered}

The course has twelve sessions and a capstone project. **When and where** each one happens is in the first table below, which is also published as a calendar you can subscribe to. **What each one covers** — its page, its main reading, its biological case study and the size of its lab — is in the second. See [Course Information & Logistics](course-info.qmd) for grading, lab policy, and how the course actually runs.

<!-- SCHEDULE-DATES -->

## When and where {#when-and-where}

All times are local (Stockholm). Everything but the project deadline happens at **SciLifeLab**, Tomtebodavägen 23A in Solna; [Session 0](session00.qmd#at-scilifelab) has the directions and what you need to get through the gates. Who teaches each lecture and lab is the current plan. The teaching assistants of each lab, and the lab quizzes themselves, are on the course's Canvas page.

**This page is the source.** Canvas shows the same events, but as a copy made when the course package was last imported into it, so between imports it can be out of date. This table and the calendar below are rebuilt from the schedule itself every time the site is published; where they and Canvas disagree, these are right.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Put the course in your own calendar

Subscribe to **<https://course.bioinfo.se/kb8029.ics>**. It updates itself: a changed room or time reaches your
calendar without you doing anything.

- **Google Calendar:** Other calendars → **+** → *From URL* → paste the address.
- **Apple Calendar:** File → *New Calendar Subscription* → paste the address.
- **Outlook:** Add calendar → *Subscribe from web* → paste the address.

Subscribe rather than import — an imported copy is a snapshot taken once and never
updated. On a phone, [webcal://course.bioinfo.se/kb8029.ics](webcal://course.bioinfo.se/kb8029.ics)
usually opens the calendar app directly.
:::

## What each session covers {#what-each-session-covers}

Three phases: bioinformatics foundations build up to profiles and protein structure (Sessions 3-6); a convergence zone (Sessions 7-9) where the classical material directly motivates and is resolved by neural networks; then a deep-learning arc (Sessions 10-12) that keeps extending the same secondary-structure-prediction thread.

**Every lab, regardless of the length noted below, is administered through Canvas, not this book** — the "Lab" column here just indicates how substantial each session's lab is, not where to find or submit it. See [Course Information & Logistics](course-info.qmd) for the general lab-quiz policy (50% correct to pass, one redo chance, each lab due the evening before the next lecture) and the course's Canvas page for each lab's actual worksheet, deadline, and submission mechanism.

| \# | Session | Primary reading (open, linked) | Biological case study | Lab |
|---------------|---------------|---------------|---------------|---------------|
| 0 | [**Introduction to the course**](session00.qmd) — how the course works, where to find everything, setting up | — | — | None (setup: VS Code and Colab) |
| 1 | [**Math prerequisites**](session01.qmd) — linear algebra, calculus, probability refresher | d2l.ai, [Preliminaries](https://d2l.ai/chapter_preliminaries/index.html) (§2.3 Linear Algebra, §2.5 Calculus, §2.6 Probability & Statistics) | — | None (non-code problem set) |
| 2 | [**Programming prerequisites**](session02.qmd) — NumPy/Matplotlib recap, notebooks, Biopython, SciPy, scikit-learn, PyTorch | [*A Byte of Python*](https://python.swaroopch.com/); d2l.ai [Preliminaries](https://d2l.ai/chapter_preliminaries/index.html) §2.1 Data Manipulation, §2.2 Preprocessing, §2.5 Automatic Differentiation; Biopython [Tutorial and Cookbook](https://biopython.org/docs/latest/Tutorial/index.html) | Real published mouse-liver RNA-seq data (Becares et al. 2019) for a real volcano plot; six real human globin genes, fetched live via `Bio.Entrez`, for the Biopython demo | **Full** |
| 3 | [**Biological Databases**](session03.qmd) | Wikipedia: [Biological database](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_database), [Sequence database](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sequence_database); NCBI: [GenBank overview](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genbank/); practice via EMBL-EBI Training's [What is ENA?](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/training/online/courses/ena-quick-tour/what-is-ena/) and [The UniProt databases](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/training/online/courses/uniprot-quick-tour/the-uniprot-databases/) | The *HBB* (beta-globin) locus | Light exercise |
| 4 | [**Sequence Alignment**](session04.qmd) | Wikipedia: [Needleman–Wunsch algorithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Needleman%E2%80%93Wunsch_algorithm), [Smith–Waterman algorithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smith%E2%80%93Waterman_algorithm), [Substitution matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substitution_matrix) (BLOSUM/PAM); practice: EMBL-EBI [Pairwise Sequence Alignment](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/training/online/courses/guide-to-sequence-analysis-tools/sequence-alignment/pairwise-sequence-alignment/) and [Multiple Sequence Alignment](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/training/online/courses/guide-to-sequence-analysis-tools/sequence-alignment/multiple-sequence-alignment/) | Aligning two homologous globins | **Full** (by-hand DP matrix + traceback, then parameter/E-value sensitivity, then a simple MSA) |
| 5 | [**Advanced Database Search & Profile Methods (BLAST, PSSMs, HMMs)**](session05.qmd) | Wikipedia: [BLAST (biotechnology)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BLAST_(biotechnology)), [Hidden Markov model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hidden_Markov_model), [Position weight matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Position_weight_matrix), [Sequence profiling tool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sequence_profiling_tool); NCBI: [BLAST® Help](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1762/) (public domain) | A real BLAST search on an unknown sequence, followed by PSI-BLAST/a Pfam domain search on the same family — framed explicitly as: a profile/PSSM score is a weighted sum over positions, i.e. already a linear model | **Full** (BLAST and profile/HMM search) |
| 6 | [**Protein Structure**](session06.qmd) | Wikipedia: [Protein structure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein_structure); [RCSB PDB-101](https://pdb101.rcsb.org/) | Hemoglobin's 3D fold in PyMOL: secondary structure (helices, strands) and tertiary structure, the structural background for Session 7's secondary-structure prediction | **Full** (PyMOL) |
| 7 | [**Linear models, gradient descent, the XOR problem & secondary structure prediction**](session07.qmd) | d2l.ai, [Linear Neural Networks for Regression](https://d2l.ai/chapter_linear-regression/index.html); Wikipedia [Perceptron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perceptron), [*Perceptrons* (book)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perceptrons_(book)), [Protein secondary structure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein_secondary_structure); [Bulyk, Johnson & Church (2002)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11861919/), *Nucleic Acids Research* 30(5):1255-1261; Rost & Sander (1993), *J. Mol. Biol.* 232:584-599 | Formalize Session 5's profile score as a perceptron, and predict the secondary structure that Session 6 introduced; show its weights can be *learned* by gradient descent instead of derived from alignment statistics; two real-world punchlines — a zinc-finger transcription factor's non-additive binding (Bulyk et al.), and Rost & Sander's PHD method solving real secondary-structure prediction the same way, at scale | **Full** |
| 8 | [**Machine learning foundations & practical PyTorch**](session08.qmd) | d2l.ai, [Linear Neural Networks for Classification](https://d2l.ai/chapter_linear-classification/index.html) + [Builders' Guide](https://d2l.ai/chapter_builders-guide/index.html) | Regression vs. classification, evaluation metrics, homology-aware splits (MMseqs2); **subcellular localization** network defined in PyTorch | **Full** (evaluating a blood-cell classifier) |
| 9 | [**How a neural network learns, and why training fails**](session09.qmd) | d2l.ai, [Multilayer Perceptrons](https://d2l.ai/chapter_multilayer-perceptrons/index.html) | Training a network on breast-cancer biopsies; why training fails (momentum and Adam); epistasis in the GB1 protein fitness landscape (when a hidden layer pays off); overfitting on protein localization; L1 and L2 regularization | **Full** (training loop on blood-cell images) |
| 10 | [**CNNs, from ImageNet to biology**](session10.qmd) | d2l.ai, [Convolutional Neural Networks](https://d2l.ai/chapter_convolutional-neural-networks/index.html) + [Modern Convolutional Neural Networks](https://d2l.ai/chapter_convolutional-modern/index.html) | ImageNet history, cancer histology with transfer learning and an image foundation model (DINOv2), biomedical imaging, DNA (DeepSEA), a learned signal-peptide filter, contact prediction | **Full** (CNNs on blood-cell images) |
| 11 | [**Sequences, language models & SignalP**](session11.qmd) | d2l.ai, [Recurrent Neural Networks](https://d2l.ai/chapter_recurrent-neural-networks/index.html) + [Attention Mechanisms and Transformers](https://d2l.ai/chapter_attention-mechanisms-and-transformers/index.html) | RNN/LSTM, attention and the Transformer, the road to GPT and BERT, protein language models as foundation models; SignalP 1.0 → 6.0 and its few-shot gain, reproduced with ESM-2 | **Full** (RNNs and ESM embeddings) |
| 12 | [**AlphaFold & generative models of protein structure**](session12.qmd) | Primary papers (AlphaFold 1-3, ColabFold, RFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN) | From coevolution to AlphaFold; complexes (pDockQ, ipTM, ipSAE); AlphaFold3 and diffusion; the four regions of interaction prediction; protein design | **Full** (AlphaFold Server, AlphaFold DB) |
| — | [**Capstone Project: Secondary Structure Prediction**](capstone.qmd) | — | Closes the loop opened at Session 6 | The project itself |
